renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: lane_composition
  title: Lane share per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a lane and each segment a library of the sample sheet, or the Undetermined reads, sized by its share of the lane's reads. It answers how evenly the lane was split between libraries and how much no index claimed.
    How to read: segments of similar size mean a balanced pool. A large Undetermined segment means indexes were misread, missing from the sample sheet or swapped, so open the unknown barcodes tile next. A library far smaller than its neighbours was under-pooled.
    Note: BCL Convert publishes no pass or fail cut-off for these shares, so none is drawn.
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    value_title: Share of the lane (%)
    x_title: Lane
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    sample_id: lane_label
    taxon: sample
    rank: level
    abundance: pct_of_lane

- component: advanced_viz
  id: lane_sunburst
  title: Lane and library hierarchy
  description: |-
    Each arc is a share of the reads of the run: the inner ring is the lane and the outer ring its libraries, sized by reads and coloured by lane. It answers how the run's reads divide between lanes and, within a lane, between libraries.
    How to read: lanes of similar width mean even loading. A library arc that is wide in one lane and thin in another points to uneven pooling or a lane problem. Use the lane composition tile to compare shares lane by lane.
  kind: sunburst
  roles:
    abundance: reads
    ranks:
    - lane_label
    - sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: library_index_purity
  title: Reads against index purity
  description: |-
    Each point is a library in one lane: its number of reads on the horizontal axis and the share of those reads whose index matched exactly on the vertical axis, coloured by lane. It answers whether low-yield libraries are also the ones with poorly read indexes.
    How to read: points should sit near the top of the plot whatever their size. A library low on the axis, or a whole lane shifted down, has many reads that only matched with a mismatch, which can signal index quality problems or index sets that are too close. Compare the lanes of the same library.
    Note: BCL Convert publishes no pass or fail cut-off for index purity, so no line is drawn.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of reads with a perfect index match of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of BCL Convert.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
    log_x: true
    x_title: Reads
    y_title: Reads with a perfect index match (%)
    top_n_labels: 3
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: reads
    y: pct_perfect_index
    label: sample
    color: lane_label

- component: figure
  title: Share of the lane per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library in one lane: the percentage of that lane's reads it received, coloured by lane. It answers which libraries are over- or under-represented.
    How to read: in an evenly pooled run the bars are close in height. Very short bars are under-pooled libraries and very tall ones dominate the lane. Check the same library across lanes to tell a pooling issue from a lane issue.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: pct_of_lane
    color: lane_label
    barmode: group
    labels:
      sample: Library
      pct_of_lane: Share of the lane (%)
      lane_label: Lane

- component: card
  title: Reads assigned to libraries
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total reads assigned to a library, leaving out the Undetermined reads, and the bars rank the lanes by their share of it. It answers how much of the run produced usable data.
    How to read: lanes of similar size mean even loading, and the median and maximum per library row show how skewed the pooling is.
  column: reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: lane_label
  top_n_count: 5
  filter_expr: col('sample') != 'Undetermined'
  caption: reads, by lane

- component: card
  title: Library share of its lane
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of a lane's reads taken by a library, and the box shows the quartiles and outliers. It answers how even the pooling is.
    How to read: a tight box means libraries were pooled evenly. A long tail of high or low values marks libraries to re-pool or re-sequence.
  column: pct_of_lane
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('sample') != 'Undetermined'
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Bases at Q30 or above per library
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of a library's bases with a quality score of 30 or higher, and the box shows the spread between libraries. It answers whether base quality is consistent across the pool.
    How to read: a tight box near the top means uniform quality. A library far below the others deserves a look at its lane and read in the base quality tile.
    Note: BCL Convert publishes no Q30 cut-off, since the expected value depends on the instrument and read length, so none is drawn.
  column: pct_q30
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('sample') != 'Undetermined'
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Demultiplexing statistics
  description: |-
    One row is one library in one lane, plus the Undetermined reads, with its reads, lane share, yield, base quality and index purity. It answers which libraries sit behind an outlier on the tiles above.
    How to read: Sort by reads or by the lane share to find the over- and under-represented libraries, and by the Q30 share or the perfect-index share to find weak ones. Look for libraries far from their lane peers and for a large Undetermined row. It complements the lane summary and the unknown barcodes tiles of the same output.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: lane_health
  title: Lane quality against Undetermined share
  description: |-
    Each point is a lane: the share of its reads that no index claimed on the horizontal axis, the share of its bases at Q30 or above on the vertical axis, sized by yield and coloured by flowcell. It answers which lanes underperform and whether the cause is quality or demultiplexing.
    How to read: healthy lanes sit at the left (little Undetermined) and high on the plot (high quality). A lane pushed to the right lost reads to indexes that matched no library, and a lane pushed down has weak base quality. Compare each lane with the others of the same flowcell.
    Note: BCL Convert publishes no pass or fail cut-off for either measure, since expected values depend on the instrument and the kit, so no line is drawn.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of bases at Q30 or above of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of BCL Convert.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
    x_title: Undetermined reads (% of the lane)
    y_title: Bases at Q30 or above (%)
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: pct_undetermined
    y: pct_q30
    label: lane_label
    size: yield_gb
    color: flowcell

- component: figure
  title: Yield per lane
  description: |-
    Each bar is a lane: its total yield in gigabases, coloured by flowcell. It answers whether the lanes produced a similar amount of data.
    How to read: lanes of a flowcell should be close in height. A short bar is a lane that lost clusters or was loaded lightly, so look at its pass-filter clusters and Undetermined share.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median yield per lane of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of BCL Convert.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: lane_label
    y: yield_gb
    color: flowcell
    barmode: group
    labels:
      lane_label: Lane
      yield_gb: Yield (Gb)
      flowcell: Flowcell
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: yield_gb

- component: card
  title: Total yield
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total yield of the run in gigabases and the bars rank the lanes by their yield. It answers how much data the run produced and which lanes carry it.
    How to read: lanes of similar size mean even loading. The median and maximum per lane show how far apart the lanes are.
  column: yield_gb
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: lane_label
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: yield, by lane

- component: card
  title: Clusters passing filter
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of clusters that passed the instrument's chastity filter, and the bars rank the lanes. It answers how many reads the run could produce.
    How to read: lanes with far fewer clusters than the median were under-clustered or lost clusters to the filter.
  column: clusters_pf
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: lane_label
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: passing-filter clusters, by lane

- component: card
  title: Lowest Q30 across lanes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest share of bases at Q30 or above of any lane, and the box shows the spread across lanes. It answers whether every lane reached good quality.
    How to read: a box that is tight and near the top means uniform quality. The hero value points at the weakest lane, which is where to look first.
    Note: BCL Convert publishes no Q30 cut-off, since the expected value depends on the instrument and read length, so none is drawn.
  column: pct_q30
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: lowest lane, with the spread

- component: card
  title: Highest Undetermined share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest share of reads no index claimed in any lane, and the box shows the spread across lanes. It answers whether a lane lost an unusual part of its reads to demultiplexing.
    How to read: a high hero value with a tight box means every lane shares the problem, usually a sample sheet or index issue. A single high lane points at that lane. Open the unknown barcodes tile to see which indexes are involved.
  column: pct_undetermined
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: highest lane, with the spread

- component: table
  title: Lane summary
  description: |-
    One row is one lane, with its clusters, yield, base quality, Undetermined share and the evenness of its libraries. It answers which lane is weak or unbalanced.
    How to read: Sort by the Undetermined share or the Q30 share to find the lanes that stand apart, and by the spread of library reads to find uneven pooling. Look for a lane that differs from the others on any of these. It complements the per-library demultiplexing table, which shows the libraries inside a lane.

outputs.name: Base quality per lane and read

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: lane_read_dots
  title: Base quality per lane and read
  description: |-
    Each dot is one read of one lane: the dot size is the fraction of its bases at Q30 or above and the colour is its mean base quality. It answers which lane and read have the weakest quality.
    How to read: large dots in a bright colour mean high-quality bases. A small or dim dot marks a read or lane to inspect, ideally compared with the same read in the other lanes.
    Note: BCL Convert publishes no Q30 cut-off, since the expected value depends on the instrument and read length, so none is drawn.
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: lane_label
    gene: read_label
    mean_expression: mean_quality
    frac_expressing: frac_q30

- component: figure
  title: Bases at Q30 or above per lane and read
  description: |-
    Each bar is one read of one lane: the percentage of its bases with a quality score of 30 or higher, coloured by read. It answers how quality compares between lanes and between reads.
    How to read: bars should be close in height across lanes. A lower bar for one lane points at a lane problem, and a lower bar for one read only points at that read.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of bases at Q30 or above of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of BCL Convert.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: lane_label
    y: pct_q30
    color: read_label
    barmode: group
    labels:
      lane_label: Lane
      pct_q30: Bases at Q30 or above (%)
      read_label: Read
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: pct_q30

- component: card
  title: Lowest Q30 across reads
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest share of bases at Q30 or above of any read and lane, and the box shows the spread. It answers whether every read reached good quality.
    How to read: a box that is tight and near the top means uniform quality. The hero value is the weakest read, which is where to look first.
  column: pct_q30
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: lowest read, with the spread

- component: table
  title: Base quality metrics
  description: |-
    One row is one read of one lane, with its yield and the share of bases at Q30 or above. It answers which read is the weakest.
    How to read: Sort by the Q30 share, lowest first, to find the weakest reads. Look for the second index read or read 2 trailing read 1, which is common as cycles accumulate. It complements the lane summary, which gives the quality of the lane as a whole.

- component: figure
  title: Most frequent unknown barcodes
  description: |-
    Each bar is an index pair BCL Convert saw among reads it could not assign: its share of the lane's reads, coloured by whether the i7 and i5 indexes belong to libraries of the lane, one panel per lane. It answers why reads were left undetermined.
    How to read: a tall bar whose two indexes are both in use is an index hop or a sample sheet swap between those libraries. One index in use points to a mistyped index, and neither in use means a library missing from the sample sheet or a contaminant.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: barcode
    y: pct_of_lane
    color: swap_class
    facet_col: lane_label
    facet_col_wrap: 2
    labels:
      barcode: Index pair
      pct_of_lane: Share of the lane (%)
      swap_class: Index status
      lane_label: Lane

- component: card
  title: Reads of the top unknown barcodes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total reads of the listed unknown barcodes and the ring splits them by whether their indexes belong to libraries of the lane. It answers what kind of problem the unassigned reads come from.
    How to read: a large share where both indexes are in use points to index hopping or a sample sheet swap. A large share where neither is in use points to missing libraries or contamination.
  column: reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - count
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: swap_class
  caption: reads, by index status

- component: table
  title: Top unknown barcodes
  description: |-
    One row is one unknown index pair in one lane, ranked by reads, with its in-use status. It answers which indexes are in the Undetermined reads and why.
    How to read: Sort by reads to start with the most frequent pairs. Look for an index pair with a swapped or in-use half, which points to a sample sheet error, and for a high-count pair that is in no sheet, which points to a missing library. It complements the lane summary, which gives the Undetermined share of each lane.
